# <a id="_4epvgmxeejf4"></a>__The Wright\-Patterson Security Breach__

[JANET RILEY](https://substack.com/@juanita4141)

Jan 19, 2026

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

In the early 90s, I was working at Wright\-Patterson Air Force Base in Dayton, Ohio\. For anyone unfamiliar with military life, these bases aren’t exactly places where information—especially phone numbers for supervisors—is just handed out\. My plan for my 40th birthday was simple: total radio silence\. I wanted to slip through the day without a single balloon, sign, or “Over the Hill” joke\.

I hadn’t counted on my husband\.

To this day, I have no idea how he managed to penetrate military security, but he successfully obtained my boss’s direct phone number\. He didn’t just call to be sweet; he called to commit a prank of international proportions\. He told my boss it was my birthday, and then, for reasons known only to him and the “Skunk” hall of fame, he told him I was turning 50\.

My boss, usually a man of order, pivoted immediately into the role of co\-conspirator\. He walked right up to me and announced, “Your husband called\. He says you’re 50 today\.”

I was indignant\. “I am only 40\!” I insisted\.

He didn’t miss a beat\. “Well, if your husband said so, he must be right\.”

“If my husband said so, it’s wrong\!” I replied, but the battle was already lost\.

The base apparently had plenty of printer ink and black crepe paper that day\. By lunchtime, signs were plastered throughout the office announcing: __“Janet is 50 Today\.”__ My desk wasn’t just decorated; it was entombed in black crepe paper\. Every surface, every drawer—a mourning ceremony for a decade I hadn’t even reached yet\.

When I finally got home, I was a whirlwind of frustration\. I started fussing at him the moment I walked through the door\. “How the heck did you manage that? My boss ran with it\! I had signs everywhere and crepe paper all over my desk\!”

I was looking for an apology, or at least an explanation for the security breach\. I got neither\. He just sat there and laughed\. It was the laugh of a man who knew he’d pulled off the impossible: he’d turned a military base into a birthday circus\.
